name: Adaptive-RAG: Learning to Adapt Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models through Question Complexity
venue: NAACL 2024 (Proceedings of the 2024 Conference of the North American Chapter of the ACL, pages 7036-7050; ACL Anthology 2024.naacl-long.389)
authors_affiliation: Soyeong Jeong, Jinheon Baek, Sukmin Cho, Sung Ju Hwang, Jong C. Park (corresponding author). All affiliated with KAIST (Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology), School of Computing and Graduate School of AI.
maintained_repo_url: N/A (single-author research repo, last pushed 2024-05; not a continuously-updated leaderboard/paper-list)
task_domain: QA (open-domain question answering, spanning single-hop and multi-hop / multi-step reasoning QA)
problem_setting: Offline, single-agent, non-interactive open-domain QA over a fixed Wikipedia-style document corpus. The system must, per incoming query, dynamically choose one of three retrieval-augmented LLM strategies (no-retrieval, single-step retrieval, or iterative multi-step retrieval) to balance accuracy and computational cost. No human-annotated complexity labels are available; supervision for the routing classifier is automatically constructed from (a) the actual prediction outcomes of the three strategies (silver labels) and (b) inductive dataset biases (single-hop datasets -> single-step, multi-hop datasets -> multi-step). The off-the-shelf LLM and retriever are frozen; only a small external classifier is trained.
what_is_retrieved: docs (Wikipedia passages / external knowledge-base documents relevant to the query)
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus (Wikipedia passages for single-hop datasets, and the preprocessed multi-hop document corpus from Trivedi et al. 2023 IRCoT). No agent-written growing memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k document ranking per retrieval call (standard BM25 top-k). The novel adaptive lever is over the NUMBER of retrieval STEPS (0 / 1 / iterative), not over recovering a complete minimal document set; not a precision-driven variable-size set.
retrieval_unit: document (Wikipedia / KB passage). Retrieval granularity is the standard passage/document returned by BM25; the adaptive component routes WHEN/HOW MANY TIMES to retrieve.
index_source: Static corpus, offline-built. Documents indexed offline in Elasticsearch/BM25 (HotpotQA 5,233,329; 2WikiMultihopQA 430,225; MuSiQue 139,416; Wiki 21,015,324 indexed documents). Store is frozen at test time.
index_structure_topology: Flat term-based inverted index (BM25 over Elasticsearch 7.10.2). No graph or hierarchical structure.
retriever_type: BM25 (term-based sparse retrieval, Robertson et al. 1994), used off-the-shelf and shared across all compared methods for fair comparison.
retriever_learning_signal: none (off-the-shelf BM25, not trained). The learned component is the separate query-complexity ROUTER classifier, not the document retriever.
query_construction: For single-step: raw input query q. For multi-step (label C): the IRCoT-style interleaved process where each retrieval step uses the original query plus accumulated Chain-of-Thought context (q, c_i) to issue the next retrieval. A separate T5-Large classifier consumes the raw query q to produce a complexity label (A/B/C) that selects the strategy.
query_granularity: Task-level for the routing decision (one classification at t=0 over the raw query). Within the chosen multi-step path, retrieval is step/CoT-step-level (iterative).
when_to_retrieve: adaptive (learned router): a trained complexity classifier selects no-retrieval (A) / single-step retrieval (B) / iterative multi-step retrieval (C) per query.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Learned query-complexity classifier (a smaller T5-Large LM outputs label o in {A,B,C}). Trained on automatically-collected labels from (1) silver data = which of the three strategies actually answered correctly, with ties broken toward the simpler strategy, and (2) inductive dataset bias (single-hop->B, multi-hop->C) for queries left unlabeled by silver labeling.
reranking: None. Standard BM25 top-k results are used directly; no cross-encoder or RRF reranking stage is introduced.
retrieved_context_refinement: None beyond strategy selection. Retrieved documents are injected directly into the LLM prompt; no decompose-recompose, distillation, distractor filtering, or compression is applied (within the multi-step path it follows IRCoT's interleaving of CoT and retrieval).
how_retrieved_used: prompt augmentation: retrieved documents are concatenated into the LLM input. Single-step uses LLM(q,d); multi-step iteratively uses LLM(q,d_i,c_i) with accumulated documents/CoT context; no-retrieval uses LLM(q) only.
planning_integration: retrieve-then-plan / per-step interleaved depending on routed strategy. Label A: direct LLM answer (no retrieval). Label B: one-shot retrieve-then-answer. Label C: iterative interleaving of Chain-of-Thought reasoning and retrieval inside a search loop (IRCoT, Trivedi et al. 2023), repeating until the reasoning chain yields the answer.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer for labels A and B (single response). Per-CoT-step for label C (multi-step IRCoT interleaves a reasoning/Chain-of-Thought step with a retrieval step each round).
retrieved_item_representation: Raw retrieved documents (Wikipedia/KB passages) inserted as text into the LLM prompt; no distillation into strategies/guidelines/programs.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw document/passage (no distilled strategy, workflow, or skill abstraction).
noise_robustness_mechanism: None explicit. The implicit robustness mechanism is the routing classifier itself: by routing simple queries to no-retrieval, it avoids injecting partially-irrelevant retrieved documents (the case study shows Adaptive Retrieval pulling distracting 'Microsoft' docs whereas Adaptive-RAG answers from parametric knowledge). No dedicated relevance evaluator, self-reflection, or distractor-aware training.
memory_type: none (no episodic/skill/workflow memory; the only learned artifact is the static query-complexity classifier).
write_back: false. No new experiences, cases, or documents are written back into any store during deployment.
online_growth: false. The document index is frozen after offline construction; nothing grows at test time.
write_back_trigger: never (no memory write-back; the classifier is trained once offline and then frozen at inference).
failure_experience_usage: Partially, only at classifier TRAINING time (offline), not as stored retrievable experience: the silver-labeling uses which strategies succeed/fail to assign complexity labels (success of the simplest strategy -> A, etc.). Queries that all three strategies fail are left to inductive-bias labeling. There is no failure memory stored or retrieved at test time.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (no stored memory entries to mutate). The classifier weights are fixed after offline training; no online update.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Partial: the WHEN/HOW-MANY-STEPS routing decision is a learned classifier (supervised cross-entropy on automatically-collected silver+binary labels), not RL. The document-selection within each step remains fixed similarity top-k BM25. So routing-as-policy is a supervised classifier, not an RL/value-based policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: N/A (single-agent, single private system; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory sharing).
benchmarks: Single-hop: SQuAD v1.1, Natural Questions (NQ), TriviaQA. Multi-hop: MuSiQue, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA. 500 test samples per dataset, evaluated jointly to simulate mixed-complexity workloads.
benchmark_family: QA (open-domain single-hop) + multi-hop QA. Single-hop family: SQuAD/NQ/TriviaQA; multi-hop family: MuSiQue/HotpotQA/2WikiMultiHopQA.
baselines: No Retrieval (LLM only); Single-step Approach (one-shot retrieve-then-read); Multi-step Approach (IRCoT, Trivedi et al. 2023, iterative CoT+retrieval, the most sophisticated SOTA); Adaptive Retrieval (Mallen et al. 2023, entity-frequency-based binary retrieve-or-not); Self-RAG (Asai et al. 2024, self-reflective adaptive retrieval, with LLaMA2-7B/13B base); plus Adaptive-RAG w/ Oracle (upper-bound oracle classifier).
key_metrics: Effectiveness: EM (Exact Match), F1, Acc (accuracy = answer contains ground truth). Efficiency: Step (number of retrieve-and-generate steps) and Time (average per-query answering time relative to the single-step approach).
headline_result: Averaged over all 6 datasets with FLAN-T5-XL (3B): Adaptive-RAG F1 46.94 / EM 37.17 / Acc 42.10 at 2.17 steps (relative time 3.60), versus the Multi-step Approach F1 48.85 / EM 39.00 / Acc 43.70 at 4.69 steps (relative time 8.81) and the Single-step Approach F1 44.31 / Acc 38.87 at 1.0 step. Adaptive-RAG nearly matches the expensive multi-step accuracy while roughly halving the number of steps, and beats the adaptive baselines (Adaptive Retrieval F1 32.24; Self-RAG* F1 20.79). With GPT-3.5 it reaches Acc 48.97 at only 1.03 steps.
ablations: (1) Classifier training data ablation (Table 4, FLAN-T5-XL): full (silver+binary) gives F1 46.94 / 1084 steps / overall classifier Acc 54.52; w/o Binary (silver only) F1 43.43 / 640 steps / Acc 60.30 but Multi-class Acc collapses to 39.55; w/o Silver (binary/inductive-bias only) F1 48.79 / 1464 steps / overall Acc 40.00 with No-retrieval Acc 0.00 - showing silver labels are needed to recover the no-retrieval (A) class and binary labels are needed for multi-hop (C) accuracy/efficiency balance. (2) Classifier size (Table 6): Small 60M (F1 45.83), Base 223M (F1 45.97), Large 770M (F1 46.94) - little sensitivity, so a small classifier suffices. (3) Adaptive-RAG w/ Oracle classifier as an upper bound (avg F1 56.28 / Acc 49.90 at 1.28 steps for FLAN-T5-XL), showing headroom for classifier improvement. (4) Confusion-matrix analysis of misclassification across A/B/C labels.
evaluation_decoupling: Yes, partially. The query-complexity CLASSIFIER is evaluated intrinsically (classification accuracy overall and per A/B/C label, plus confusion matrix in Figure 3 and Table 4) separately from the end-to-end QA metrics (EM/F1/Acc). However, this is classifier accuracy, not retrieval Recall@k/nDCG (retrieval quality itself is not separately scored).
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both. Outcome: QA EM/F1/Acc. Process: number of retrieval-and-generate steps, per-query time, classifier complexity-prediction accuracy, and per-label classification breakdown - i.e., the routing/process quality is explicitly measured alongside final answer quality.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Central focus. Reports Step count and relative Time per query, plus exact per-query latency (Table 3): No(A) 0.35s, One(B) 3.08s, Multi(C) 27.18s, with predicted label distribution 8.60% A / 53.33% B / 38.07% C. Adaptive-RAG cuts steps from the multi-step approach's 4.69 to 2.17 (FLAN-T5-XL) while retaining near-multi-step accuracy; with GPT-3.5 it uses only 1.03 steps vs 2.81 for multi-step.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k BM25 retrieval per step (following IRCoT/Trivedi et al. 2023 implementation details for prompts and document counts). The adaptive budget is at the STEP level (0/1/iterative retrievals), not at the per-query token-k level; multi-step terminates per IRCoT stopping criteria.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (this is a method paper, not a survey).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing benchmarks rather than constructing a new one). Note: 500 test samples per dataset are subsampled following Trivedi et al. 2023; classifier training uses ~400 sampled queries per dataset annotated via silver + inductive-bias labels.
builds_on: IRCoT (Trivedi et al. 2023, used as the multi-step strategy and as the skeleton code base); standard single-step retrieve-then-read RAG; BM25 (Robertson et al. 1994); FLAN-T5 (Chung et al. 2022) and GPT-3.5 as frozen reader LLMs; T5-Large (Raffel et al. 2020) as the classifier; DPR Wikipedia corpus (Karpukhin et al. 2020).
contrasts_with: Adaptive Retrieval (Mallen et al. 2023, binary entity-frequency retrieve-or-not - too coarse, ignores multi-hop); Self-RAG (Asai et al. 2024, single self-reflective model that retrieves/critiques/generates - argued to be either overly simple or overly complex for all queries); Qi et al. 2021 (fixed retrieve-read-rerank loop on BERT-like LMs needing task-specific training); always-multi-step and always-single-step one-size-fits-all RAG.
lineage: Sits in the lineage of adaptive / when-to-retrieve RAG (Group B: RAG for task solving). It is a router-based bridge between no-retrieval, single-step RAG, and iterative multi-step RAG (IRCoT/FLARE/Self-RAG family), pioneering the use of a learned query-complexity classifier to select retrieval depth; widely featured downstream in LlamaIndex/LangGraph adaptive-RAG recipes.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a case-based-reasoning method; no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain case cycle).
explicit_cbr_grounding: false. The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is an adaptive retrieval-routing framework.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tool/skill retrieval; retrieves plain documents).
index_content_separation: N/A (no lightweight-index-then-content separation; standard BM25 index over full passages).
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (static document index; no tool API / RapidAPI / MCP / function-calling integration).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no tools, no inter-tool dependency modeling).
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (no case adaptation; retrieved documents are used verbatim as prompt context).
